text: Given valid placeholder credential headers, When the agent calls initialize then tools/list, Then all 17 watchguard_* tools are returned with the documented names, and tools/call watchguard_get_account (mocked 200) returns the account payload, not an error envelope
evidence: pytest -v: test_tools_list_returns_full_catalog PASSED (asserts 17 tool names == full catalog); test_get_account_success_returns_payload PASSED (respx-mocked 200, result.data == {"accountId":"WGC-1-000000","name":"Acme MSP"}, no error key). Also verified live over HTTP: started `python -m watchguard_mcp` and curled initialize+tools/list with placeholder headers -- HTTP 200, 17 watchguard_* tools returned (no Mcp-Session-Id sent, confirming stateless per SOP SS1.3). Full suite: 18 passed, 0 failed.

text: Given no accountId argument and no X-WatchGuard-Account-Id header, When watchguard_get_account is called, Then it resolves to the credential owner's own account and never substitutes any other account id
evidence: pytest -v: test_get_account_defaults_to_credential_owner_account PASSED. Mocked /oauth/token returns a token carrying claim account_id=WGC-1-OWNER; GET /v2/accounts/WGC-1-OWNER mocked 200 and asserted called exactly once; result.data matches that payload; and /v1/audiences route asserted call_count == 0 (never called, so no other account's audience/id is ever substituted). Implementation note: this relies on the WatchGuard token response carrying an account identifier claim (tech design Decision 6) -- unconfirmed against a live account, flagged as 'needs a real vendor account' like TC9.

text: Given any one of X-WatchGuard-Access-Id / X-WatchGuard-Password / X-WatchGuard-Api-Key is missing, When any watchguard_* tool is called, Then the server returns HTTP 401 whose body names exactly the header that was omitted, with no fallback to environment variables
evidence: pytest -v: all three PASSED, each asserting resp.status_code == 401 and missing_headers == [exactly the one omitted header]. Also verified live: curl POST /mcp with no WatchGuard headers at all returned HTTP 401 with body {"error":"missing required header(s)","missing_headers":["X-WatchGuard-Access-Id","X-WatchGuard-Password","X-WatchGuard-Api-Key"]} (both local run and the built linux/amd64 container).

text: Given X-WatchGuard-Account-Id is set to a managed account id, When a tool is called, Then the client calls POST /v1/audiences before POST /oauth/token, and the resulting token request includes the returned audience value
evidence: pytest -v: test_managed_account_id_resolves_audience_before_token PASSED. Asserts audience_route.call_count==1, token_route.call_count==1, token request body contains 'audience=aud-xyz', and the recorded call order has /v1/audiences before /oauth/token.

text: Given mocked vendor responses of 404 / 429 / 500, When a tool call hits each, Then the result is the structured envelope with code not_found / rate_limited / upstream_error respectively, and 429/500 are retried at least once (honoring Retry-After on 429) before the final envelope is returned
evidence: pytest -v: all three parametrized cases PASSED (envelope code matches; 429/500 assert account_route.call_count >= 2, i.e. retried). test_retry_delay_honors_retry_after_header PASSED, asserting WatchguardClient._retry_delay reads the Retry-After header value (7.0s) directly rather than falling back to the exponential default. Real sleeping is skipped in tests via the fast_backoff fixture (monkeypatches the _backoff_sleep indirection), so the retry *logic* is exercised without slowing the suite; the real 1s/2s backoff schedule runs unmodified outside tests.

text: Given watchguard_delete_account or watchguard_delete_operator is called without the required id argument, When invoked, Then it is rejected with an invalid_argument envelope (no wildcard/all form exists), and both tools' schema marks destructiveHint true
evidence: pytest -v: all three PASSED. test_delete_account_requires_account_id / test_delete_operator_requires_identifiers call with an empty-string id and assert the returned envelope's error.code == 'invalid_argument'. test_delete_tools_are_marked_destructive lists tools via the in-memory Client and asserts annotations.destructiveHint is True for both watchguard_delete_account and watchguard_delete_operator.

text: Given a mocked operator create response carrying a transaction_id, When the tool returns, Then the result includes that transaction_id, and watchguard_get_operator_transaction_status called with it returns the mocked final status
evidence: pytest -v: both PASSED. test_create_operator_returns_transaction_id asserts result.data parses to a payload containing transaction_id == 'txn-123'. test_transaction_status_tool_returns_final_state asserts the polling tool's result matches the mocked {"transaction_id":"txn-123","status":"completed"}.

text: Given two concurrent requests carrying different X-WatchGuard-* credentials, When their tool calls interleave, Then neither request ever reads the other's ContextVar-held credentials, and there is no module-level or global cache of tokens or account data
evidence: pytest -v: test_concurrent_requests_do_not_share_context_var PASSED. Four concurrent asyncio-gathered requests, each with distinct X-WatchGuard-Access-Id/X-WatchGuard-Account-Id pairs, are asserted to each read back only their own pair via the request-scoped ContextVar -- no cross-contamination across the 4 interleaved calls. Code review note: WatchguardClient is constructed fresh per tool invocation (client_factory() in server.py) and closed via its own async context manager; nothing is cached at module scope anywhere in client.py/context.py.

text: Given a real WatchGuard Cloud account, When live calls are made to watchguard_get_account, watchguard_activate_device, and watchguard_create_operator, Then each returns live vendor data matching the documented response shapes
steps: Obtain a real WatchGuard Cloud account's Access Id, Password, and Api Key (Manage Access page)
Set X-WatchGuard-Access-Id / X-WatchGuard-Password / X-WatchGuard-Api-Key on the request
Call watchguard_get_account with no accountId argument
Call watchguard_activate_device with a real activation key (only against a vendor test/trial account, never assumed to exist)
Call watchguard_create_operator with a disposable test operator
expect: Each call returns a 200-shaped tool result matching the documented WatchGuard response fields, not an error envelope
evidence: No WatchGuard Cloud test/trial account is available to this pipeline; not a blocker for publishing to INT per SOP 'no test account is not a blocker' and mcp-track.md section 3 completion criteria. Listed in the dev report as 'needs a real vendor account'. Additionally untested for the same reason: the token-claim-based own-account resolution (TC2's implementation note) and the exact vendor request/response field names used throughout client.py (accountId/name/licenseKey/etc. are the best-supported reading of the fetched API docs, not confirmed byte-for-byte).
